content: Suicide Exclusion: In case of death due to suicide within 12 months from the date of commencement of risk or from the date of revival of policy, the nominee or beneficiary of the policyholder shall be entitled to receive at least 80% of the total premiums paid till the date of death or the surrender value available as on the date of death, whichever is higher, provided the policy is in force.

The policyholder has a period of 30 days (for policies sourced electronically or via distance marketing) and 15 days (for physical policies) from the date of receipt of the policy document to review the terms and conditions. If disagreed, the policyholder may cancel by stating the reasons, receiving a full refund of premiums paid less proportionate risk premium, medical examination expenses, and stamp duty.

A grace period of 30 days is allowed for payment of yearly, half-yearly, and quarterly premiums. For monthly premium payment mode, a grace period of 15 days is allowed. The policy remains in full force during the grace period. If premium remains unpaid at the expiry of the grace period, the policy lapses.

Human Life Value (HLV) & Financial Underwriting: Life insurance coverage is capped as a multiple of verified annual income based on applicant age. For applicants aged up to 35 years, maximum cover is restricted to 25x annual income. For ages 36-45, cover is limited to 20x annual income. For ages 46-55, cover is limited to 15x annual income. Any cover exceeding these limits mandates 3 years of audited ITR-V, Form 16, and financial justification.

Special Exit Value (Zero-Cost Exit): The policyholder can terminate the policy and receive a complete refund of all total premiums paid (excluding taxes and rider costs) provided the policy is active, the applicant has attained age 65 or completed 25 policy years, and the exit option is exercised within the designated window before policy termination.

Riders and Supplementary Benefits: Critical illness cover and Accidental Death Benefit (ADB) riders are optional add-on protections and are not covered under pure term base rates. Adding comprehensive critical illness coverage or accidental death protection requires additional actuarial premium loading over the standard pure term base rate.

As per individual life insurance tax regulations, individual pure term life insurance premiums enjoy a 0% effective GST rate for individual policyholders, and qualify for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act up to statutory limits.
